title: Nanoscale Stripe Domain Structures in Ferroaxial RbFe(MoO4)2
content: Ferroaxial or ferro-rotational order is a recently recognized type of ferroic order that emerges from rotational distortions within structural units and is defined by a rotational electric-dipole moment linked to the ferroaxial moment A∝∑iri×pi, where ri is the position of the electric dipole pi relative to the symmetric center of the structural unit (Fig 1a) [1-6]. The distinctive properties of ferroaxial materials, particularly the couplings among structural ferroaxiality, magnetic chirality, and electric polarization, which lead to unique magnetoelectric effects [4,6,7], has recently broadened the scope of research to explore their domain structures and the manipulate these domains via external fields [7,8]. Macroscopic detection of ferroaxial domain structures has been achieved through second harmonic generation [9-11], electrogyration [12], X-ray diffraction [13], neutron diffraction [14], and optical microscopy [15]. These photon-based methods offer broad statistical insights into ferroaxial domains but lack the spatial resolution to discern fine nanoscopic details. Moreover, since these imaging methods are generally conducted along the crystallographic c-axis or the ferroaxial rotation axis, three-dimensional domain structures still remain elusive.
